good-christian-men-rejoice.sources: // Sources: song file (the parts' guide notes, checked with arranger-keep/partfacts.py: pitches by time sung, every top and bottom note on its own syllable); licence.source for the book

parts.soprano: Carries the old German tune as Neale and Helmore's book of 1854 prints it, most often on F, then C and A, up to its top D four times a verse: on the middle one of the three notes of "joice" and of "voice;", on "ye" in "Give ye heed" ("Now ye hear", "Now ye need") and on "and" in "Ox and ass" ("hath" in "He hath oped", "you" in "Calls you one,"), and down to its low D only on "Christ is" at the start of each verse's closing "Christ is born to-day! Christ is born to-day!" ("Christ was" in verses 2 and 3).
parts.alto: Sings the words under the tune, mostly a sixth or a third below it, most often on E, then C and D, up to its top F five times a verse: on "ye" in "Give ye heed" ("Now ye hear", "Now ye need") and on "what" in the same line (the "end-" of "endless", "fear"), on the "day:" of "born to-day:" just before "Ox" ("this!" before "He", "save!" before "Calls"), and on "and" and the "fore" of "before" in "Ox and ass before him bow," ("hath" and the "heav'n-" of "heav'nly" in verse 2, "you" and the second "calls" in verse 3), and down to its low A only on both "day!"s at the end of each verse ("this!" in verse 2, "save!" in verse 3).
parts.tenor: Sings the words in the middle of the chord, most often on A, then G and F, up to its top C seven times a verse: on "ian men," and "and soul," in the first two lines, on the same C as the alto, on the first word of the third line ("Give", "Now"), on the "day:" of "born to-day:" ("this!", "save!" in verses 2 and 3) and on "Ox" ("He", "Calls") after it, and down to its low C only on the song's very last note, the last "save!".
parts.bass: Sings the bass line, most often on F, then C and D, up to its top F on many notes, among them every note of "Good Christian men, re-" at the start of each verse, and down to its low F, an octave lower, only on the song's very last note, the last "save!".

parts_es.soprano: Lleva la antigua melodía alemana tal como la imprime el libro de Neale y Helmore de 1854, con más frecuencia en el Fa, luego en el Do y el La, sube a su Re agudo cuatro veces por estrofa: en la nota central de las tres de "joice" y de "voice;", en "ye" de "Give ye heed" ("Now ye hear", "Now ye need") y en "and" de "Ox and ass" ("hath" de "He hath oped", "you" de "Calls you one,"), y baja a su Re grave solo en "Christ is" al comienzo del "Christ is born to-day! Christ is born to-day!" que cierra cada estrofa ("Christ was" en las estrofas 2 y 3).
parts_es.alto: Canta la letra por debajo de la melodía, sobre todo una sexta o una tercera por debajo, con más frecuencia en el Mi, luego en el Do y el Re, sube a su Fa agudo cinco veces por estrofa: en "ye" de "Give ye heed" ("Now ye hear", "Now ye need") y en "what" del mismo verso (el "end-" de "endless", "fear"), en el "day:" de "born to-day:" justo antes de "Ox" ("this!" antes de "He", "save!" antes de "Calls"), y en "and" y el "fore" de "before" en "Ox and ass before him bow," ("hath" y el "heav'n-" de "heav'nly" en la estrofa 2, "you" y el segundo "calls" en la estrofa 3), y baja a su La grave solo en los dos "day!" del final de cada estrofa ("this!" en la estrofa 2, "save!" en la estrofa 3).
parts_es.tenor: Canta la letra en el centro del acorde, con más frecuencia en el La, luego en el Sol y el Fa, sube a su Do agudo siete veces por estrofa: en "ian men," y "and soul," de los dos primeros versos, en el mismo Do que la contralto, en la primera palabra del tercer verso ("Give", "Now"), en el "day:" de "born to-day:" ("this!", "save!" en las estrofas 2 y 3) y en el "Ox" ("He", "Calls") que lo sigue, y baja a su Do grave solo en la última nota de la canción, el último "save!".
parts_es.bass: Canta la línea del bajo, con más frecuencia en el Fa, luego en el Do y el Re, sube a su Fa agudo en muchas notas, entre ellas todas las de "Good Christian men, re-" al comienzo de cada estrofa, y baja a su Fa grave, una octava más abajo, solo en la última nota de la canción, el último "save!".
